chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from one of our companions, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace bequeathed from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'What a good mosque is the Mosque of Kufa; a thousand Prophets and a thousand Successors have prayed in it. From it burst forth the oven (of Noah), and therein was built the ship. Its right side is the Pleasure of Allah, and its middle is a garden from the gardens of Paradise, and its left side is Makr.'

So I said to Abu Baseer: 'What does he mean by his word 'Makr'?' He said: 'He means the houses of the Sultan (ruling authority). And the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) would stand at the door of the mosque, then he would shoot his arrow, and it would fall in the place of the date-sellers, so he would say: 'That is from the mosque (part of its area).'
And he (peace be upon him) would say: 'There has been reduced from the foundation of the mosque the like of what was reduced regarding its four corners.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and historical significance of the Mosque of Kufa according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi underscores the spiritual and historical prestige of the Grand Mosque of Kufa, identifying it as a locus of prophetic continuity where a thousand prophets and Imams prayed, and linking it to Noahic history. The Imam clarifies that 'Makr' refers to the ruler's residence, citing Imam Ali’s practice of marking the boundary with an arrow, while noting the structural diminution of the mosque's foundation and corners, a detail often interpreted by Shia scholars as reflecting the political and physical encroachments on the sacred space over time.
